$comment: Table Derby admin contract v9. Generated by packages/contracts/scripts/emit-admin-contract.mjs from packages/contracts/src/admin.ts, adminContent.ts, adminOps.ts, adminReleases.ts and adminIntegration.ts; do not edit. Pin a copy and compare this version.
pagination: A paged list takes ?cursor= and ?limit= (1 to 200, default 50) and answers { items, nextCursor }; pass nextCursor back as cursor until it is null. Cursors are opaque.
time: Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC. Days (dates, the dashboard, the ticket top-up) are Georgian: Asia/Tbilisi, UTC+4, no daylight saving.
concurrency: A write that sends a version (a correction, a setting) applies only at that version; otherwise 409 revision_conflict with details.current, the record as it is now.
strings: String rules are ECMAScript patterns applied with the u flag, so lengths are in code points; values are never trimmed (send them trimmed); the API lower-cases emails after checking them. No format keyword is used: the patterns decide. fixtures/validation-cases.json lists what must be accepted and refused.

auth.accessToken: Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>; audience td-admin; about 15 minutes
auth.session: 12 hours from sign-in, or 1 hour without a refresh
auth.refresh: Rotating refresh tokens. A retry of the same request (same token and requestId) within retryWindowMs, while its successor is unused, gets the same successor; a later retry is refused (invalid_refresh_token) without ending the session; a spent token under another requestId, or none, revokes the whole session (refresh_token_reused). See fixtures/refresh-scenarios.json.

types.name: Card
types.about: Round I cards (approved with their category)

types.name: BoxQuestion
types.about: Round III questions (approved with their category)

types.about: Images (credit, licence and source optional): exactly one of uploadId (an upload) and url (an image kept from before), the other null

content.workflow: draft → ready (mark ready, any member) → approved (publisher and up, their own last edit included). Any change to the data or the position is a new content version (order is part of a release): a ready or approved row goes back to draft, keeping its approved content and position (what a release carries) until it is approved again. The note alone changes no version. draft, ready or approved → archived (publisher and up; an editor only their own draft, never approved and never written to by anyone else; never deleted); archived → approved when its content is the version approved, draft otherwise. Every write names the version (the row revision) it read: another is 409 revision_conflict with the row as it is now. Every change is in the row history. Two writes that meet in the database may end in 409 conflict_retry: send the same request again.
content.references: Rows refer to others by key: cards and box questions to their category, a practice question to its image (media), a career path to clubs, the calendar and the cycle to puzzles. Approving a category approves the listed cards or questions with it and needs every other live one approved; approving or restoring a row needs what it refers to in releases: an image or club with an approved version, not archived, and a puzzle with a question whose approved content is in it; a pending edit to what is referred to holds nothing up (the release carries its approved content). An image, a club or the last approved question of a scheduled puzzle that live content uses is not archived.
content.imports: preview judges each item on its own (nothing is written); import creates every item as a draft in one step, or none (422 validation with the report); the same batchKey with the same items answers again without adding anything. Undo removes the rows still at the revision the import created (no change since, not even a note or a ready) and never approved, and keeps the others with the reason.

media.uploads: POST /admin/media/uploads takes the image itself as the body (Content-Type image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp; at most 2 MB and 4096 pixels a side; checked by its bytes and decoded) and keeps it private. A media row uses it by uploadId, with its width and height; new images are uploads (an image by URL is only one kept from before, and its URL cannot change). An image is approved by a publisher; its licence, credit and source are optional.
media.publishing: A published release shows each uploaded image from its re-encoded WebP copies, 480 and 960 pixels wide, in the public bucket, under names that say nothing of the image. Cards may show an uploaded photo (imageKey) instead of their face, clubs an uploaded crest (crestImageKey).

releases.validate: POST /admin/releases/validate: what publishing the approved content now would give; errors refuse a publish (schema, pool sizes for a match, 30 days of dailies from today in Georgia, images that cannot be shown), warnings do not.
releases.publish: POST /admin/releases/publish {idemKey} (publisher and up) starts a publication and answers 202 (200 for the same key again, whatever it has done since); poll GET /admin/publications/:id. One publish or rollback runs at a time (409 publication_in_progress names it). Its phases run on the server and resume after any restart; a failed one removes what it made. The pointer moves only from the version the snapshot saw (pointer_moved otherwise).
releases.rollback: POST /admin/releases/:id/rollback {idemKey} (publisher and up): back to an available release that was current before and still serves every daily game today.

routes.consumes: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp, as the raw body (at most 2 MB, 4096 pixels a side)

routes.produces: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp: the image as sent

AdminRefreshRequest.description: POST /admin/auth/refresh. One random requestId (a UUID) per refresh, kept for all its retries.

AdminLogoutRequest.description: POST /admin/auth/logout. Any refresh token of the session ends all of it.

PasswordChangeRequest.description: POST /admin/auth/password (signed in). Ends every session of the member and returns a fresh one.

StaffInviteRequest.description: POST /admin/staff/invite. The API lower-cases the email; role "ops" passes the schema but is refused (403); an email still invited is invited again.

StaffPatchRequest.description: PATCH /admin/staff/:id. Role, status, or both; at least one.

AdminTokenResponse.description: Login, refresh, accept-invite, reset and password change. expiresAt is the access token's expiry.

LinkTokenResponse.description: A single-use link token (48 h) to hand over; never emailed by the API.

AdminError.description: Every refusal. Branch on code; message is human text and may change.

ContentActor.description: A member, or the system (id null: the seed).

ContentListQuery.description: The query of every content list: status (a comma list; default all but archived), q (text search), category (a category key for cards and box questions, the label for practice and Football Logic), puzzle, game, from and to (the calendar), sort (natural, updated, created), dir, cursor, limit (1–200, default 50).

ContentPageQuery.description: The query of the import list and of a row history: cursor, limit (1–200, default 50).

ContentHistory.description: GET /admin/content/:type/:id/history: a row's changes, newest first (by the id of its trail entry). Rows an import undo removed keep their history.

ContentTransitionRequest.description: Mark ready, archive, restore: at the version read.

ContentApproveRequest.description: Approve at the version read. A category approves the listed cards (or questions) with it, at their versions; every other live one must be approved already.

ContentImportItem.description: One import item: a row of a type, created as a draft. Rows refer to rows before them by key.

ContentImportPreviewRequest.description: POST /admin/content/imports/preview: items as ContentImportItem, each judged on its own.

ContentImportRequest.description: POST /admin/content/imports: the previewed items under a key the client chose (the same key with the same items is the same import; with other items, 409 conflict).

ContentImportReport.description: What an import would do, item by item (preview; the details of a refused import).

ContentImportBatchSummary.description: An import batch, without its rows.

ContentImportBatch.description: An import batch and the rows it created, in item order. Undo removes rows still at the version it created and never approved; it keeps the others and says why.

ContentImportResult.description: POST /admin/content/imports: created is false when the key was applied before.

RevisionConflictDetails.description: details of 409 revision_conflict: the row as it is now (as GET returns it), and the listed child whose version moved, if one did.

ValidationDetails.description: details of 422 validation: the problems, by path.

DependencyDetails.description: details of 409 dependency_unapproved: what must be approved first.

PageQuery.description: The query of a paged list: cursor (the previous page’s nextCursor) and limit (1–200, default 50).

PlayerSearchQuery.description: GET /admin/players query: q is a nickname prefix (any case), a partner player id or a player id.

AdminPlayerList.description: GET /admin/players: matching players by nickname, a page at a time.

AdminLedgerList.description: GET /admin/players/:id/tickets: the ticket ledger, newest first.

AdminMatchRecord.description: GET /admin/matches/:id, and the answer to a correction. A match voided after Redis lost its state has no inputs (inputs.missing says why). Inputs go to the archive 180 days after the match (inputs.archivedAt) and are read back from it; missing is archived when the archive cannot be read just now, and expired once it is deleted (730 days after the match).

MatchCorrectionRequest.description: POST /admin/matches/:id/corrections: version is the resultVersion read; a winner must be one of the match’s players.

SnapshotCreateRequest.description: POST /admin/leaderboard/snapshots (betsson_admin and ops). Labels are unique, whatever the case.

Snapshot.description: A frozen leaderboard: never changed or deleted.

SnapshotPage.description: GET /admin/leaderboard/snapshots/:id: the snapshot and a page of its rows by rank.

CsvExport.description: A CSV download (text/csv; charset=utf-8): a UTF-8 BOM, a header row, RFC 4180 quoting, and a leading apostrophe on any text cell a spreadsheet could read as a formula.

Dashboard.description: GET /admin/dashboard, in Georgia time (Asia/Tbilisi, UTC+4): today and yesterday; the last 7 and 30 days (today so far and the 6 or 29 days before it; null until the daily rollup has reached every day of the period before yesterday); and a point per day for the last 30, oldest first.

Settings.description: GET /admin/settings and the answer to a change (ops only).

TicketsPerDayRequest.description: PATCH /admin/settings/tickets-per-day: version is the one read (0 if never set).

MaintenanceRequest.description: PATCH /admin/settings/maintenance: version is the one read (0 if never set).

OpsReview.description: A penalty to review: an early self-forfeit penalised under an allowance count a correction later lowered. Closed by a correction of its match, or dismissed.

ReviewListQuery.description: GET /admin/reviews query: status open (the default) or all, cursor, limit.

OpsRevisionConflictDetails.description: details of 409 revision_conflict on a correction or a setting: current is the record or the settings as they are now.

MediaUpload.description: An uploaded image in private storage, for a media row to use (MediaData.uploadId, with its width and height). width and height are as displayed (EXIF orientation applied).

ImageRefusalDetails.description: details of 422 invalid_image: type (not JPEG, PNG or WebP, or not what the Content-Type says), signature (the bytes are not an image of those), trailing_data (more than the image), dimensions (over 4096 pixels a side), animated, decode (it does not decode).

ReleaseReport.description: POST /admin/releases/validate, and a publication’s snapshot: errors refuse a publish, warnings do not. An image needs no credit, licence or source: media.missingRights only counts those without.

PublicationRequest.description: POST /admin/releases/publish and POST /admin/releases/:id/rollback: a key the client chose, kept for every retry of this request (a UUID will do). The same key answers the same publication.

Publication.description: A publish or a rollback, run in phases on the server (poll GET /admin/publications/:id until status is published or failed). One runs at a time. A publish: snapshot, validate, media, artifact, available, pointer; a rollback: pointer only (the rest skipped).

PublicationBusyDetails.description: details of 409 publication_in_progress: the publication holding the slot.

ReleaseListQuery.description: GET /admin/releases query: cursor (the previous page’s nextCursor) and limit (1–200, default 50).

ReleaseList.description: GET /admin/releases: the pointer, the publication under way (if any), releases newest first, the latest 50 pointer moves.

ReleaseDetail.description: GET /admin/releases/:id: what it holds, its rows, and what changed against the release current before it.

DailyPublishRequest.description: POST /admin/dailies/:game/publish: whole days (puzzles) to publish. Each must have exactly the day size of its game (footballLogic 10, putInOrder 4, careerPath 10) live questions.

DailyPublishResponse.description: In one transaction (publisher and up): the days’ questions are approved (each day then has exactly its size of approved questions); today keeps the day players get now (a schedule entry pins it; 503 busy while the current release cannot be read; an approved entry already on today is left as it is); the calendar is read from approved entries, and a date holding a draft or archived entry gets it back; each day that never had a date gets the next free one after the last; the cycle becomes every dated day in date order, then the days it repeated already (none drops out; when that is more than 400 days, the last 400), anchored the day after the last date, so after the calendar the days repeat from the first. Days already dated never move. Running it again changes nothing. Players get it with the next release.

WebhookListQuery.description: GET /admin/integration/webhooks query: q (an event id, a partner session id, the partner’s player id or a Table Derby player id), status, cursor, limit.

WebhookRetryRequest.description: POST /admin/integration/webhooks/:id/retry (ops): {} to retry now; retarget: true also moves an event bound to an earlier webhook address to the current one. Either way its 24 hours of retries start again.

WebhookEvent.description: A result event for the partner and where its delivery stands: pending (retried with backoff for 24 hours), sent (the partner answered 2xx) or dead (given up; retry it now to try again).

WebhookAttempt.description: One delivery attempt: the HTTP status the partner answered, or why there was no answer (error), its latency and the start of the answer.

WebhookEnvelope.description: The result event exactly as it is sent to the partner (partner contract §4); its data depends on its type.

WebhookEventDetail.description: GET /admin/integration/webhooks/:id (the event id) and the answer to a retry: the event, the envelope sent and its latest 200 attempts, oldest first.
